guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our disagreement with the market is modest, and we are not dismissing Ohio State’s ability to create separation. We see substantial offensive continuity: Ohio State returned eight starters on that side of the ball and 85.8 percent of its offensive-line snaps from 2025. The 671-yard opener reinforces the upside of that group, but we are not treating one result against Ball State as proof that every opponent should be priced the same way.

The matchup profile also makes it difficult for us to support Illinois aggressively. Our numbers show a major advantage for Ohio State’s passing offense against the Illinois pass defense, while Illinois faces difficult paths both running the ball and creating scoring opportunities against Ohio State. Those are meaningful concerns when taking this many points because Illinois may struggle to sustain enough offense to stay within range.

The counterweight in our view is turnover on the Ohio State defense. Only three defensive starters returned, with eight lost from the 2025 unit. We saw Ohio State hold Ball State to 165 yards in the opener, but that single performance does not fully resolve the uncertainty surrounding a reworked group. That helps explain why our model lands a little closer than the market, but the disagreement is not large enough for us at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
For us, the matchup to watch is Ohio State’s passing game against the Illinois secondary. Julian Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns in 2025, and our efficiency numbers again rate this passing offense among the nation’s best. Illinois’ pass-defense profile is the clearest reason our lean toward the underdog does not become a wager.

We also saw Jeremiah Smith catch eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half of the opener. We are not extrapolating that stat line directly, but it illustrates the explosive receiving threat Illinois must contain. If Ohio State consistently generates efficient early-down throws, the market’s expectation of a wide margin becomes much easier to justify.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 home win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Against Ball State, Ohio State produced 671 total yards: 434 passing and 237 rushing.
Ohio State held Ball State to 165 total yards, including 45 rushing and 120 passing.
Ohio State converted 45.5 percent of its third downs and held Ball State to a 21.4 percent third-down conversion rate.
Fourteen Ohio State players caught a pass against Ball State, the program's first game with at least 14 receivers recording a catch since Sept. 22, 2018 against Tulane.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns, all in the first half, against Ball State.
Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry against Ball State and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen against Ball State.
Freshman Legend Bey had 100 all-purpose yards against Ball State and scored on his first career reception.

opponent_notes.fact: Ohio State is scheduled to host Illinois on Sept. 26, 2026; the game time and television assignment were not yet announced in this guide.
Ohio State cornerback Devin Sanchez recorded a 2025 season-high five tackles and a pass breakup against Illinois.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin is a returning offensive starter and entered 2026 with 15 starts in 19 career games.
In 2025, Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes, threw for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns with eight interceptions, and ranked second nationally with a 177.5 efficiency rating.
Sayin's 77.0 percent completion rate in 2025 set Ohio State and Big Ten single-season records.
Sayin has seven career 300-yard passing games.
Backup quarterback Justyn Martin entered 2026 with six career game appearances and no starts.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned eight offensive starters: quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Bo Jackson, receivers Jeremiah Smith and Brandon Inniss, tackle Phillip Daniels, center Carson Hinzman, and guards Luke Montgomery and Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Ohio State returned 85.8 percent of its 2025 offensive-line snaps among players who logged at least 100 snaps, the highest listed rate among Power Four teams.
After the 2026 opener, Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts.
The returning offensive linemen included Carson Hinzman with 36 career starts, Austin Siereveld with 21, Phillip Daniels with 17 and Luke Montgomery with 17.
Bo Jackson rushed for a team-high 1,090 yards on 179 carries in 2025 and had six 100-yard games in his first 12 appearances.
Jeremiah Smith entered the second game of 2026 with 171 career receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.
Receiver Devin McCuin transferred from UTSA after recording 65 receptions for 726 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025.
Receiver Kyle Parker transferred from LSU with 34 career receptions for 385 yards and five touchdowns across 21 games and seven starts.
Ohio State's returning tight ends included Hunter Welcing with 11 career starts, Bennett Christian with two and Nate Roberts, who appeared in 13 games as a freshman.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned three defensive starters from 2025: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters: tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.
Defensive tackle James Smith transferred from Alabama after recording 28 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks in 2025.
Defensive end Qua Russaw transferred from Alabama with 50 career tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, two sacks and two interceptions.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro transferred from Wisconsin with 127 career tackles and eight sacks across 36 games and 12 starts.
Defensive tackle John Walker transferred from UCF with 64 career tackles, eight tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks in 26 games.
Safety Earl Little Jr. transferred from Florida State after leading FSU with 76 tackles in 2025; he entered Ohio State with 97 career tackles and four interceptions.
Safety Terry Moore brought 19 career starts from Duke, while Little brought 13 career starts and defensive linemen James Smith and John Walker each brought at least 12.
Kenyatta Jackson Jr. recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025.
Jaylen McClain was Ohio State's sixth-leading tackler in 2025 with 53 tackles and played 816 defensive snaps.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen serves as run game coordinator and offensive line coach, Billy Fessler as pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Keenan Bailey as co-offensive coordinator and tight ends coach.
Cortez Hankton coaches wide receivers, Carlos Locklyn coaches running backs, Larry Johnson coaches the defensive line and James Laurinaitis coaches linebackers.
